Class RadioGroup<T>

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.RadioGroup<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the value type (typically an enum)
public final class RadioGroup<T> extends Object
The lens a set of Radio buttons shares: which value is selected, read from the consumer every frame and written back when the player picks another (§0026, §0066). It stores nothing. 
RadioGroup<Mode> mode = RadioGroup.state(() -> config.mode, m -> config.mode = m);
Radio.builder(mode, Mode.FAST).label(Component.literal("Fast")).build();
Radio.builder(mode, Mode.SAFE).label(Component.literal("Safe")).at(0, 14).build();

Not an element. The group holds no Radios, and Radios are not its children: each lives in a panel like any other element and asks the group whether its value is the selected one. The group is wiring only, which keeps "a Panel is the ceiling of composition" true.

Values are compared with Objects.equals(Object, Object), so they should implement equals (enums do). A get that returns null selects no Radio.
